CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Analysis of fetal tissue following pregnancy loss

SPECIMEN TYPE
Uncultured placental material

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 21, 22, X and Y. DNA was extracted from uncultured placental tissue. PCR amplification was performed followed by capillary electrophoresis on an ABI 3500 Genetic Analyzer. Peak area ratios were calculated to determine chromosome copy number. A minimum of 4 informative markers per chromosome were analyzed where possible.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13: Three alleles detected (trisomic pattern)
Chromosome 14: Four alleles detected (tetrasomic pattern)
Chromosome 15: Three alleles detected (trisomic pattern)
Chromosome 16: Three alleles detected (trisomic pattern)
Chromosome 18: Three alleles detected (trisomic pattern)
Chromosome 21: Three alleles detected (trisomic pattern)
Chromosome 22: Three alleles detected (trisomic pattern)
Sex chromosomes: XXY pattern detected

SUMMARY: Abnormal male karyotype consistent with triploidy (69,XXY) with additional tetrasomy for chromosome 14

INTERPRETATION
QF-PCR analysis reveals three copies of chromosomes 13, 15, 16, 18, 21 and 22 with an XXY sex chromosome complement, indicating triploidy. Additionally, four copies of chromosome 14 were identified, representing an unusual finding of tetrasomy 14 in the setting of triploidy.

Triploidy is a lethal chromosomal abnormality incompatible with survival and is a common cause of first trimester pregnancy loss. The presence of an additional copy of chromosome 14 (tetrasomy 14) represents a sporadic chromosomal error that further compromised fetal viability.

The combination of triploidy with additional chromosome 14 aneuploidy explains the pregnancy loss. The chromosome 14 abnormality is considered sporadic and unlikely to recur in future pregnancies.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Parental karyotyping is not indicated as these findings represent sporadic chromosomal errors
2. Ultrasound monitoring is advised for future pregnancies
3. Prenatal diagnosis (CVS or amniocentesis) is available for reassurance in future pregnancies
4. Clinical monitoring is recommended due to the small risk of gestational trophoblastic disease if molar changes were present in the placenta
5. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss these results and implications for future pregnancies

The recurrence risk for triploidy is approximately 1-1.5%, not significantly increased above the general population risk.

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: Dr. [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
